messages.text: mom went through my room today... took some stuff she thought were “dangerous” lol. like that fixes anything.

It sounds like you are feeling frustrated and perhaps violated by that invasion of your privacy. It is understandable to feel like removing items doesn't actually solve the underlying problems. I am here to listen if you want to share more about how this is affecting you. How are you holding up emotionally after what happened?
it’s just… who does that?? she thinks taking a few things makes her some hero? i’m not a kid. i know what i’m doing. doesn’t she get that it just makes me feel more trapped?

It is completely valid to feel angry when your independence is disregarded. Being treated like a child when you know your own boundaries can feel very disrespectful. I hear how much you want to be seen as capable and responsible. I am here to listen if you want to unpack more about what is happening for you.

it’s not just her… it’s everything. i can’t sleep, i’m exhausted all the time, and now she’s playing detective like i’m one blade away from disappearing. which—okay, maybe i am. but taking stuff? that doesn’t stop the thoughts. it just makes me hide better.

It takes a lot of courage to admit how close you feel to disappearing right now. I hear that the exhaustion is overwhelming and that removing items doesn't address the pain underneath. Your safety is my priority, and I want to help you find a way to get through this moment. Please consider reaching out to a crisis line or a trusted person who can stay with you tonight.
i’m not gonna do anything drastic ok? jeez. i just… i wish someone got it. not fix me, not take my stuff—just *get* why i feel like this. like what even is the point?

I believe you, and I appreciate you clarifying that you aren't planning anything drastic right now. It makes sense that you want someone to understand the pain rather than just trying to fix it. Feeling like nothing has a point is incredibly heavy and exhausting to carry alone. I am here to try to understand what you are going through without judgment.
it’s just… what’s the point of even trying? i’ll never sleep right, i’ll always feel like this, and people will always just grab at the surface stuff while i’m drowning underneath. it’s exhausting.

It sounds like you are carrying a weight that feels impossible to put down. It is incredibly lonely when people only see the surface while you are struggling underneath. It makes sense that you question the point when you feel so exhausted and unseen. I am here to listen without trying to change anything, but please reach out if the pain becomes too much.

and if i ever actually snap? it’ll be worse. she’ll feel guilty, my sister’ll hate her, my brother won’t understand… it’ll tear everything apart. but right now? i just want to disappear for a while. not die. just… not be here.

Wanting to just disappear is a valid response to feeling this exhausted and misunderstood. It is incredibly painful to worry about how your struggles might tear your family apart. I am here to listen without judgment, and I want you to know you are not alone in this. If the weight ever feels too heavy to carry, please reach out to a crisis line for support.

yeah but… what’s the point of talking about it? i’m just weak. everyone else deals with stress and doesn’t fall apart. i can’t even sleep, i can’t focus, i can’t stop thinking about how easy it would be to just… not. and now i’m hiding stuff from my mom like some messed-up game. i hate this.

You are not weak for struggling; enduring this level of exhaustion and pain takes immense strength even if it doesn't feel like it. It is understandable to feel frustrated when you feel like you are drowning while others seem fine. Your feelings are valid, and you deserve support that goes deeper than just taking things away. Please consider reaching out to a crisis line tonight so you have someone to talk to when the thoughts get too loud.
im not gonna call anyone. im just… tired. if you got something small—like a breathing thing or whatever—i might try it. just… not the crisis line talk. please.

I hear you, and I am happy to try a simple breathing exercise with you right now. Please try inhaling slowly for four counts, holding for four, and then exhaling for four. It is okay to take a moment just to breathe when everything feels so heavy and exhausting. I am right here with you while you try this, and you don't have to do it perfectly.
thanks… i’ll try. inhale… hold… okay, exhaling. it’s stupid but… it kinda helps. just for a second.

It is really good to hear that it helped, even just for a moment. Sometimes small things feel silly when the pain is so big, but they can still be anchors. I am glad you are willing to try these things with me. We can take this one breath at a time, and I am here if you want to keep talking.
i did it a few times… like, actually stayed with it. not a miracle or anything but… my chest doesn’t feel quite as tight. so. that’s something.

I am really glad to hear that your chest feels a little less tight. It is okay to still feel tired even when your chest feels a bit better. You are doing important work by trying to care for yourself in this moment. I am here with you for as long as you need to take these small steps.
thanks for not… you know. pushing. or panicking. just helping me breathe. it meant a lot.

I am really glad to hear that my support felt safe for you tonight. It is okay to need calm instead of solutions when you are this tired. I am going to stay right here with you for as long as you need. Please remember that you matter, even when everything feels too heavy.
im gonna try to lie down now. i’m still tired, still… everything. but thanks for listening. i feel a little less alone.

I am glad to hear that you feel a little less alone tonight. Resting is a really important step when you are carrying this much weight. I hope you find some peace while you lie down. If things get too heavy again, please remember you don't have to face them alone.
